messages:
Sam: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — token-validator accepted stale refresh tokens during a cache eviction race. Root cause is the validator returning success for in-flight cache misses.
Alex: Ack. Thanks for the summary. Can we capture concrete owners and cutover dates?
Sam: Yes. I sketched a remediation plan in the meeting, copying it here. Short list first: 1) Force immediate secrets rotation window for affected clients, 2) Harden token validation path with strict DB fallback + optimistic cache invalidation, 3) Add audit-log flags on all token validation endpoints, 4) Add synthetic tests for cache-race pattern, 5) Update runbook and postmortem with recurrence indicators.
Priya: I can own secrets rotation. Plan: notify customers tonight (opt-in), rotate tokens by 2026-03-30, and provide a rollback plan. Will open a ticket and link it here. @Sam remind me what scope of clients are affected?
Sam: Affected: hosted API tokens issued between 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-22 that hit the token-validator at high QPS (approx 12k requests/min). I'll paste the query for list in the ticket.
Maria: I'll take audit logging and the validator changes (DB fallback + explicit TTL checks). Target PR by 2026-04-06, then canary deploy on dedicated pool.
Alex: I'll own synthetic tests and monitoring — add a churn detector for token validation latency spikes and failed DB fallbacks. Tests live in infra/tests/token_race/**. Can we add a daily job that simulates a cache-eviction sequence?
Sam: yes, Alex. Add the job and an alert: "token-validator.cache-race-rate > 0.1%". If triggered, auto-open a P1 incident.
Priya: Ticket created: INF-4127 — "Secrets rotation: stale-token cohort". Notes: planned rotation window 2026-03-29 00:00 UTC -> 2026-03-30 04:00 UTC, contact ops@redwood for immediate rollbacks.
Maria: Created PR: https://git.internal/redwood/token-validator/pulls/128 — adds DB fallback path + explicit cache-invalidation hook. PTAL.
infra-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary: token-validator v2.3.1 -> canary on dedicated-1 at 2026-04-07T02:00Z
Sam: Action item table (owner / deliverable / due):
- Priya / Secrets rotation + customer comms / 2026-03-30
- Maria / Validator code + audit logging / 2026-04-06
- Alex / Synthetic tests + monitoring alert / 2026-03-31
- Sam / Postmortem updates + recurrence analysis / 2026-04-02
- Security team / Full audit & KMS review / 2026-04-09
Alex: One more ask — can we add an automated check in the CI that fails if token-validator PRs remove DB fallback? Put a small grep or unit test that asserts fallback logic exists.
Maria: I'll add a unit test and an integration test. Example check in CI: ```assert config.get('token_validator.enable_db_fallback') == True```
Sam: Longer-term suggestions from the meeting: 1) rotate short-lived tokens by default, 2) expose token-introspection metrics to customer dashboards, 3) create a small chaos test that evicts cache nodes randomly during high QPS.
Priya: I'll coordinate the customer comms template with legal + support. Draft by 2026-03-25 EOD.
security-bot: Issue SEC-981 opened: "Authz token validation audit and KMS key rotation" assigned to Security. SLA: 14 days.
Sam: Recurrence note: this pattern (cache fallback + race) showed up in two prior incidents (late 2025 and early 2026) — logging showed identical stack traces. We should add a recurring incident column in the postmortem template to capture whether the root cause is systemic.
Alex: Agree. I'll propose a small schema change to postmortem template: add fields "recurrence_count", "similar_incident_links", and "mitigation_permanence".
Priya: For trackers: update the remediation tracker spreadsheet row with links: INF-4127, PR-128, SEC-981, and canary schedule.
Sam: Thanks everyone. Plan for a short sync Friday 09:00 UTC to close blockers and confirm rotation completed. If anyone can't make it, please post status in this thread. :thumbsup:
